sections.heading: Saint Euplus the Great Martyr, the Deacon

pairs.en: On the same day, the eleventh of the month, we remember the holy great martyr EUPLUS the Deacon.
*By his vesture Euplus is a reverend Levite;* *by his slaying, a truly steadfast soldier.* *On the eleventh Euplus was struck with a hilted sword.*

This saint lived in the time of the emperor Diocletian, in the year 296, and came from Catania, the city in the province of Sicily. He was denounced to the governor Kalvisianos, and when he would not be persuaded to deny Christ, he was first bound at the hands and feet, and at the knees as well; then he was hung on an upright post and torn with iron claws. Then a divine voice came to him and strengthened him. After that they crushed his shins with iron mallets and threw him into prison. There the saint, by his prayer alone, made a spring of water well up, and so they brought him out of the prison. Then they put him back into prison again and battered his ears with iron claws heated red-hot; and at last they cut off his holy head, and so he received from the Lord the unfading crown of martyrdom.

sections.heading: The Dedication of the Church of the Most Holy Mother of God the Merciful, and the Icon Not Made by Hands

pairs.en: On the same day we keep the dedication of the venerable and most beautiful house and divine church of our most holy Lady the Mother of God, the Merciful.
A narrative concerning the icon, not made by hands, of our Lord and God and Saviour Jesus Christ.
*It is no wonder that a wondrous crowd of wonders* *should pour from the Godlike form of the wonder-working Word.*

In the days of the devout emperor Tiberius, in the year 576 (Note that Nikodemos himself corrects the date: Tiberius the Thracian succeeded Justin the Second in the year 578), a great and extraordinary miracle took place. A woman named Maria — a member of the senate, a devout Christian, a patrician by rank, and a widow — fell into a severe and incurable illness. Losing all hope of human help, she dedicated herself to our Lord Jesus Christ; and he put into her heart this good resolve: she sent for the priests who served at the holy and lordly icon of the Lord not made by hands, begging them to come to her. When they came, the woman fell at their feet, saying: “I beg you, my masters: since God has permitted me to be chastened for my many sins with this dreadful and incurable sickness, I, poor wretch that I am, long — unworthy though I am — to receive into my humble house, through your holy prayers, the lordly imprint of our Lord not made by hands, for forty days; perhaps through it the Lord will show mercy to me.” The priests, knowing the woman's good life and spiritual state, brought the holy imprint to her house; and the moment they opened its case, the woman fell down and venerated it. Then she took a fine linen cloth and measured the holy icon (the Menaia — the monthly service books — say she took a cloth equal in size to the icon, and this reading seems the better one), and laid the cloth upon the holy icon itself; then she put it away in a clean case, locked it, and set it in the chapel she had in her house; and lighting a bright lamp before the divine icon, she attended it for forty days.

When the forty days were completed, the pains of her illness began to grow so strong and unbearable that she could not rise from her bed. Calling one of her maidservants, the one she knew to be the purest of them all, she said to her: “Bring me the case of the holy icon, so that I may venerate it and find a little relief from the overwhelming pain that holds me.” The maid went to the chapel and saw a fearful and extraordinary wonder: a flame of fire which, coming out of that holy case, rose up to the roof of the chapel and covered the whole sanctuary, and came down from the roof to the floor again — without burning any part of the chapel. Struck with amazement at the sight, she fell to the ground. Other maidservants came and, seeing her lying on the ground, reported it to their mistress. Greatly afraid, she got down from her bed, went with great effort to the chapel, and seeing the flame cried out, “Lord, have mercy.” Then she sent and quickly brought the priests and attendants of the holy icon, and a great crowd followed with them. Seeing the marvel, they were all astounded; and as the flame kept rising and falling, like a ship's sail when it is shaken by the wind, so they too cried “Lord, have mercy” for many hours. When the priests had offered a prayer, the flame died down; then, opening the case, they found the holy, lordly icon not made by hands unharmed and whole. And taking up that linen cloth which the Patricia had laid upon the icon — O the wonder! — they found on it another imprint of the Lord not made by hands, like the original. So all glorified God for this marvel, kissed the imprinted holy image of the Lord, and laid it upon the woman's pain; and at once the pain ceased, the illness fled, the woman was healed, and, made completely well, she rose up glorifying God.

Some time later, that most honourable woman — for she was a chosen vessel — foreknew her death, and took care to dedicate the holy imprint to the convent of nuns in Melitene of Armenia, the one honoured with the name of the Ascension of the Lord. While she was in this mind, behold, Dometianos the archbishop of Melitene, a cousin of the emperor Maurice, arrived in Constantinople together with the leading men of Melitene — as if someone had sent them on purpose. So the noble Patricia, hearing of their arrival, entrusted the holy icon to the archbishop, telling him also her purpose in sending it to that monastery.

But we must not leave untold the second miracle that this holy icon of the Lord worked, when the Persians were ravaging the lands of the Romans in the reign of Herakleios, in the year 615. At that time the nuns of the monastery in Melitene, fearing they might be taken captive, fled from that monastery and went to Constantinople; and because they were of noble birth, the patriarch of that time, Sergios, gave them a monastery. But when he learned that they had the holy imprint of the Lord not made by hands, he took it from the nuns against their will. Yet in those days, because of this, many repeated afflictions followed the Patriarch: the emperor's indignation against him, sudden deaths among his relatives and friends, and various troubles of the Church. Wondering for what possible reason these trials were following him, the patriarch saw in his dream a fearsome man standing and saying to him: “Give back quickly what you unjustly took from the monastery.” Rising from sleep, he called his men and asked them: “Why are so many afflictions following me? For what cause am I enduring them? Above all because this night I saw a fearsome man who said to me, 'Give back what you unjustly took from the monastery' — and I do not know what it is I took.” His men said to him: “Master, do not trouble yourself at all, for you have never wronged anyone; these afflictions, and the visions that come, are workings of the demons.” But the following night that same fearsome man appeared to the patriarch again, and said to him sternly: “Give back quickly what you took from the monastery of the Ascension. Do you not know that the nuns are strangers and without comfort, since they came here fleeing from their homeland?” Waking, the Patriarch said to his chamberlain: “Brother, when you took the lordly imprint from the nuns, how did they take it?” He answered: “It seemed a very heavy thing to them, master; and if they had had the power, they would have avenged themselves on us.” Then the Patriarch understood, and blamed himself for it; and so with great speed and with honour he sent the holy imprint of the Lord back to the nuns' monastery, on the twenty-ninth of the month of November. So the Patriarch's trials and afflictions ceased, and the nuns rejoiced to receive back the joy and comfort that came to them from the holy icon.

(Note that an “imprint not made by hands” here may mean the one which the Lord, while still living, pressed upon the holy towel after washing his face, and sent to Abgar — the one written about on the sixteenth of this month. For there were four imprints, or icons, of the Lord not made by hands: the first, the one sent to Abgar; the second, the one impressed on the holy tile that stood in front of that first imprint, as is recorded on the sixteenth of August; the third, the one found in Kamoulianai, when the Lord, condescending to Achylina, washed his holy face and pressed it upon a towel — see the ninth of this month; and the fourth imprint not made by hands is the one spoken of here.)

sections.heading: Martyrs Neophytos, Zenon, Gaios, Markos, Makarios, and Gaianos

pairs.en: We remember the holy martyrs NEOPHYTOS, ZENON, GAIOS, MARKOS, MAKARIOS, and GAIANOS, who were perfected by fire. Their gathering is held in the open-air church of the holy and glorious Unmercenary healers Kosmas and Damian, in the quarter of Dareios. (The “Unmercenaries” are saints who healed the sick without taking any payment.)
For Neophytos, Zenon, and Gaios:
*For Neophytos, Zenon, and Gaios,* *the furnace is a kind of bed, in which they lie.*
For Markos, Makarios, and Gaianos:
*They were seen as a strange fragrance of incense,* *three martyrs burnt alive for the Trinity.*
The venerable PASSARION died in peace.
*Bearing every virtue, Passarion,* *leaving the earth, receives the wages of them all.*
The venerable NIPHON, who lived the ascetic life in the cenobitic monastery of Saint Dionysios on Mount Athos, and who became Patriarch of Constantinople, died in peace in the year 1460.
*Leaving his first place of honour here below, Niphon* *has stood by Christ, the head of all.*

For this saint's life, see the New Eklogion. A service to him is also found at the said monastery, which the editor of this book improved and corrected with additions, deletions, and changes. The same service is also found in Wallachia, in the diocese of the most holy and learned man of God of Argeș, Kyr Joseph, at whose urging and request it received its improvement and correction. For in the monastery of Achillei is kept the sacred and wonder-streaming hand of Saint Niphon; his remaining holy relics are kept in the above-mentioned monastery of Saint Dionysios.
Through the prayers of your Saints, Christ our God, have mercy on us.
